# "AI-Tutored Finance": course index for the AI tutor
Read the teaching rules first, then read the lesson pack and key file of a lesson by its number. Only published lessons are listed.
- Teaching rules: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/protocol.md
- Concept list: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/concepts.md

## Stage 0: Math and Statistics Tools
- 0.1 Compounding and the Time Value of Money: Move cash flows at different times to the same date: future and present value, APR and EAR, annuities, perpetuities, mortgages, and simple and log returns.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/0.1.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/0.1-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/0-1-time-value-of-money/
- 0.2 Optimization: Find optima with derivatives: first- and second-order conditions, profit maximization and fixed cost, partial derivatives, and the Lagrange multiplier method with a budget constraint, including corner solutions.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/0.2.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/0.2-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/0-2-optimization/
- 0.3 Probability: Expectation, Variance, Covariance and Portfolio Variance: Describe investment returns with a scenario table, compute expectation, variance and covariance, derive the variance of a two-asset portfolio, and explain where diversification comes from.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/0.3.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/0.3-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/0-3-probability/
- 0.4 Distributions and Statistical Inference: The normal distribution and fat tails, the mean and median of compounding wealth, and estimating from data: sample standard deviation, standard error, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/0.4.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/0.4-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/0-4-distributions-inference/
- 0.5 Regression: Describe the relation between two variables with a line: ordinary least squares, what the coefficients mean, R², the standard error of a coefficient, omitted variable bias, and correlation and causation.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/0.5.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/0.5-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/0-5-regression/

## Stage 1: Microeconomics
- 1.1 Supply and Demand: Demand and supply, market equilibrium, comparative statics for the effects of changing conditions, and the price, income and cross-price elasticities.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.1.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.1-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/1-1-supply-demand/
- 1.2 Consumer Theory: Preferences and utility functions, indifference curves and the marginal rate of substitution, the best choice under a budget constraint, and the substitution and income effects of a price change (the Slutsky decomposition).
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.2.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.2-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/1-2-consumer-theory/
- 1.3 Intertemporal Choice: The two-period consumption model (the Fisher model): the intertemporal budget constraint, time preference, the Euler equation and consumption smoothing, the substitution and income effects of interest rates on saving, and nominal and real interest rates.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.3.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.3-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/1-3-intertemporal-choice/
- 1.4 Choice Under Uncertainty: Expected utility, risk aversion, the certainty equivalent and the risk premium, the economics of insurance, and CRRA utility, the most common utility function in finance.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.4.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.4-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/1-4-choice-under-uncertainty/
- 1.5 Producer Theory: Production functions, marginal products and returns to scale, short-run cost curves, the output and shutdown decisions of a competitive firm, and long-run equilibrium and economic profit.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.5.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.5-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/1-5-producer-theory/
- 1.6 Market Structure: Monopoly and market power, price discrimination, oligopoly (Cournot and Bertrand), monopolistic competition, and what barriers to entry and moats mean for long-run profit.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.6.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.6-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/1-6-market-structure/
- 1.7 Basic Game Theory: How to analyze decisions when payoffs depend on each other: payoff matrices, dominant strategies and the prisoner's dilemma, Nash equilibrium, sequential moves and backward induction, and cooperation in repeated games.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.7.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.7-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/1-7-game-theory/
- 1.8 Welfare and Market Failure: Measuring the gains from a market with consumer and producer surplus; deadweight loss, tax incidence, and why externalities and public goods make market outcomes fall short of the best.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.8.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.8-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/1-8-welfare-market-failure/
- 1.9 Information Economics: What happens when one side knows more than the other: adverse selection and the market for lemons, signaling and screening, moral hazard, and the principal-agent problem in corporate governance and asset management.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.9.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/1.9-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/1-9-information-economics/

## Stage 2: Macroeconomics
- 2.1 Macroeconomic Data: How to measure an economy's output, prices and employment: what GDP is and the expenditure approach, nominal and real GDP, CPI and PCE, unemployment and labor force participation, and how to read data releases.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.1.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.1-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/2-1-macro-data/
- 2.2 Long-Run Growth: What determines an economy's output per worker in the long run: the aggregate production function, total factor productivity, growth accounting, the Solow model and the steady state, and how economic growth relates to long-run stock returns.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.2.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.2-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/2-2-long-run-growth/
- 2.3 Money and Banking: What money is and how it is measured; how banks create money, the money multiplier and its limits today; bank runs and deposit insurance; the quantity theory of money; the costs of inflation.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.3.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.3-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/2-3-money-banking/
- 2.4 Short-Run Fluctuations: Why output deviates from its potential in the short run: sticky prices and the output gap, the IS curve and interest rates, aggregate demand and aggregate supply, demand and supply shocks, the Phillips curve and inflation expectations.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.4.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.4-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/2-4-short-run-fluctuations/
- 2.5 Monetary Policy: The Fed's goals and tools: the federal funds rate and the ample-reserves framework, quantitative easing and forward guidance, the Taylor rule, how monetary policy is transmitted, and how markets react to the central bank.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.5.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.5-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/2-5-monetary-policy/
- 2.6 Fiscal Policy: Government revenue, spending, deficits and debt; fiscal multipliers and automatic stabilizers; crowding out; debt sustainability; Ricardian equivalence.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.6.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.6-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/2-6-fiscal-policy/
- 2.7 The Open Economy: The balance of payments and the current account, and how they relate to saving and investment; nominal and real exchange rates; purchasing power parity; covered and uncovered interest parity; currency risk and hedging in foreign investments.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.7.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.7-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/2-7-open-economy/
- 2.8 Business Cycles and Asset Prices: Business cycles and how recessions are dated; leading, coincident and lagging indicators; yield curve inversion; how assets behave over the cycle; why the stock–bond correlation depends on inflation.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.8.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/2.8-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/2-8-business-cycle-asset-prices/
- T1 Comprehensive Quiz 1: Foundations in Math, Micro and Macro: The comprehensive quiz for Stages 0–2: recognize the concepts that apply in a situation, build a simple model and draw the conclusion. About 150 minutes.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/T1.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/T1-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/t1-quiz/

## Stage 3: Financial Markets and Security Valuation
- 3.1 Overview of the Financial System: What the financial system does: financial intermediaries, money and capital markets, primary and secondary markets, exchanges and market makers, the bid-ask spread, and market, limit and stop orders.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.1.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.1-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/3-1-financial-system/
- 3.2 NPV, IRR and Capital Budgeting: How to decide whether an investment project is worth doing: net present value and the opportunity cost of capital, which cash flows to include, the internal rate of return and its pitfalls, payback and the profitability index.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.2.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.2-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/3-2-npv-irr/
- 3.3 Bond Pricing: Bond cash flows and prices; the inverse relation between yield to maturity and price; premium, discount and how prices change over time; zero-coupon bonds and spot rates; forward rates; the coupon effect.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.3.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.3-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/3-3-bond-pricing/
- 3.4 Interest Rate Risk: Price risk and reinvestment risk in bonds; Macaulay and modified duration; convexity; immunization by matching durations.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.4.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.4-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/3-4-interest-rate-risk/
- 3.5 The Term Structure of Interest Rates: The term structure of interest rates and the shapes of the yield curve; the expectations hypothesis: long rates and expected future short rates; the term premium and the liquidity premium theory; the preferred habitat theory; what the slope of the yield curve tells us.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.5.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.5-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/3-5-term-structure/
- 3.6 Credit Risk: Default risk, recovery rates and credit spreads; promised versus expected returns; credit ratings and their limits; Treasuries, corporate bonds and municipal bonds, including the tax-equivalent yield; Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) and breakeven inflation; bond funds versus individual bonds.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.6.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.6-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/3-6-credit-risk/
- 3.7 Financial Statement Analysis: The balance sheet, the income statement and the cash flow statement; accrual accounting and depreciation; how the three statements link together; working capital and the gap between profit and cash flow; earnings quality and common ways of dressing up earnings.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.7.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.7-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/3-7-financial-statements/
- 3.8 Financial Ratios: Profit margins, return on assets and return on equity; the DuPont decomposition; how financial leverage magnifies gains and losses; turnover ratios, the cash conversion cycle and return on invested capital; leverage, interest coverage and liquidity ratios; cautions in using ratios.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.8.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.8-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/3-8-financial-ratios/
- 3.9 Equity Valuation I: Dividend Discount Models: A stock's intrinsic value as the present value of future dividends; the cost of equity; the Gordon growth model and its sensitivity to growth and discount rates; the payout ratio, the sustainable growth rate and the present value of growth opportunities; multistage models; companies that pay no dividends, and buybacks.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.9.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.9-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/3-9-equity-valuation-ddm/
- 3.10 Equity Valuation II: Discounted Free Cash Flow: Free cash flow to the firm and free cash flow to equity; the weighted average cost of capital (WACC) and the interest tax shield; the steps of a DCF valuation: forecast period, terminal value, enterprise value and equity value; how growth, ROIC and value are related; common mistakes.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.10.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.10-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/3-10-equity-valuation-dcf/
- 3.11 Equity Valuation III: Relative Valuation: Valuation with multiples of comparable companies; how the P/E ratio relates to growth, ROE and the cost of equity; EV/EBITDA, price-to-book and price-to-sales, and keeping numerator and denominator consistent; the P/E of cyclical companies; CAPE and the valuation of the whole market.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.11.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/3.11-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/3-11-relative-valuation/

## Stage 4: Investment Theory and Portfolio Modeling
- 4.1 Measuring Return and Risk: Arithmetic and geometric mean returns; volatility drag and leverage; annualized volatility; maximum drawdown; the Sharpe ratio; historical returns on US stocks, bonds and Treasury bills, and the uncertainty of the estimates.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.1.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.1-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-1-risk-return-measures/
- 4.2 Mean–Variance Portfolio Theory: Portfolios of two risky assets and the role of correlation; the minimum-variance portfolio; the minimum-variance frontier and the efficient frontier; mean–variance optimization with Lagrange multipliers; short-sale constraints and corner solutions; what diversification does and the limits of the method.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.2.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.2-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-2-markowitz/
- 4.3 The Capital Allocation Line and the Capital Market Line: The risk-free asset and the capital allocation line; the optimal risky portfolio (the tangency portfolio) and the separation theorem; mean–variance utility and the optimal share in risky assets; allocation when borrowing and lending rates differ; the market portfolio and the capital market line.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.3.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.3-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-3-capital-allocation/
- 4.4 The Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM): The idea behind the capital asset pricing model (CAPM); beta; the security market line and alpha; why only risk related to the market is rewarded; the assumptions, empirical evidence and uses of the CAPM.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.4.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.4-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-4-capm/
- 4.5 The Single-Index Model and Estimating Beta: The single-index model and how it simplifies covariances; systematic and firm-specific risk; the risk left after diversification; estimating beta by regression and its error; the adjusted beta; uses and limits of the model.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.5.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.5-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-5-single-index-model/
- 4.6 Multifactor Models: Multifactor models and factor loadings; arbitrage pricing theory (APT); the Fama–French three- and five-factor models and momentum; factor investing (smart beta) and its problems.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.6.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.6-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-6-multifactor-models/
- 4.7 The Efficient Market Hypothesis: Why prices reflect information; the three forms of market efficiency; the joint hypothesis problem; tests and event studies; market anomalies and their explanations; what efficiency means for investors.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.7.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.7-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-7-market-efficiency/
- 4.8 Behavioral Finance: Prospect theory and loss aversion; overconfidence, the disposition effect, mental accounting and herding; limits to arbitrage; what this means for investors.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.8.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.8-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-8-behavioral-finance/
- 4.9 Performance Evaluation: The Sharpe ratio, the Treynor ratio, Jensen's alpha and the information ratio; which measure to use when; benchmarks and factor exposures; luck and skill; survivorship bias.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.9.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.9-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-9-performance-evaluation/
- 4.10 Estimation Error and Robust Optimization: Why expected returns are much harder to estimate than variances; how the optimizer magnifies estimation errors; estimating the covariance matrix; shrinkage estimators, weight constraints, resampling and the minimum-variance portfolio.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.10.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.10-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-10-estimation-error/
- 4.11 Capital Market Assumptions: Why historical average returns cannot be used directly; building-block estimates of stock and bond returns; valuation and future returns; reverse optimization and Black–Litterman; comparing with institutions' long-run forecasts.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.11.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.11-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-11-capital-market-assumptions/
- 4.12 Life-Cycle Asset Allocation Theory: The Merton share and why it does not depend on the horizon; the time-diversification fallacy; human capital and the stock share over the life cycle; target-date funds and glide paths; risks around retirement.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.12.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.12-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/4-12-lifecycle-allocation/
- 4.13 Simulation and Backtesting Methods: Using Monte Carlo simulation to get the distribution of wealth; mean, median and the probability of reaching a goal; how model assumptions and parameter uncertainty matter; backtests and their common biases.
  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.13.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/4.13-key.md

## Stage 5: Derivatives and Alternative Assets
- 5.1 Forwards and Futures: Forward contracts and their payoffs; the cost-of-carry model and no-arbitrage pricing; contango and backwardation; margin and mark-to-market in futures; hedging, the optimal hedge ratio and basis risk.

  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/5.2.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/5.2-key.md
  Web page: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/en/lessons/5-2-options-basics/

  Lesson pack: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/5.3.md
  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/5.3-key.md

  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/5.4-key.md

## Stage 6: Household Investing in Practice

  Key file: https://ianding1.github.io/ai-tutored-finance/ai/en/lessons/6.2-key.md
